viscosity.footnote: ν = μ / ρ  ·  1 cSt = 1 mm²/s  ·  1 cP = 1 mPa·s. Water at 20 °C ≈ 1 cP ≈ 1 cSt.

gasProps.title: Gas Property Estimator
gasProps.warnPapay: Papay Z is extrapolated outside its validity envelope (Pr = {pr}, Tr = {trv}; valid 0 < Pr ≤ 15, 1.05 ≤ Tr ≤ 3.0). All four outputs depend on Z.
gasProps.warnLge: Viscosity is outside the Lee-Gonzalez-Eakin experimental basis ({tf} °F, {psia} psia; fitted over 100–340 °F and 100–8,000 psia).
gasProps.warnBelowAbsoluteZero: Temperature is at or below absolute zero.
gasProps.footnote: Screening estimates, not standards. Z uses Papay (1968) with Standing-Katz pseudo-criticals — the same routine as the Z-Factor Estimator. μ uses Lee, Gonzalez & Eakin (1966), a published correlation fitted to four sweet natural gases over 100–340 °F and 100–8,000 psia (≈2.7 % AAE); it carries no H₂S/CO₂/N₂ correction, so treat sour or high-inert gas as indicative only. c = √(k·Z·R·T/M) is the real-gas form used in API 520 for critical flow; it neglects the (∂Z/∂P)_T and (∂Z/∂T)_P terms. μ_JT is exact thermodynamics wrapped around Papay's ∂Z/∂T and an ideal-gas C_p = kR/(k−1) — positive means cooling on expansion. Gas MW = SG × 28.9647.

steam.title: Steam Properties (IAPWS-IF97)
steam.subcoolNote: {dt} K below saturation at this pressure
steam.nearSatNote: within 0.1 % of the saturation line — a real stream here is almost certainly two-phase; single-phase values shown
steam.satR3Note: h_f/h_g above 16.529 MPa lie in Region 3 — not computed
steam.satSupercritNote: supercritical — no saturation line above 22.064 MPa
steam.warnRange: Outside IF97 Regions 1/2 — valid 0–800 °C (273.15–1073.15 K), 0 < P ≤ 100 MPa
steam.warnRegion3: Region 3 (dense/near-critical) not covered — use full IF97 or vendor steam tables
steam.footnote: IAPWS-IF97 (Revised Release, 2007), Regions 1 (compressed liquid), 2 (steam) and 4 (saturation line) — the same industrial formulation behind commercial steam tables. All 259 coefficients are carried verbatim from the Release and re-verified in CI against its own computer-program verification tables (Tables 5, 15, 35, 36) to 9 significant figures. Valid 0–800 °C and up to 100 MPa; Region 3 (dense/near-critical, roughly 350–590 °C above 16.5 MPa) is out of scope — the card says so rather than extrapolating. Saturation enthalpies h_f/h_g are Region 1/2 values at T_sat(P), available up to 16.529 MPa. Btu(IT) conversions: 1 Btu/lb = 2.326 kJ/kg exactly; 1 Btu/(lb·°R) = 4.1868 kJ/(kg·K) exactly.

npsh.title: Pump Suction — NPSHa
npsh.fillHint: Writes saturated-water Pv and ρ_f at T into the two fields (overwrite freely for other liquids).
npsh.breakdownNote: pressure head + static − friction, in the output unit
npsh.warnSurfaceFlash: P_surface ≤ Pv — the liquid is boiling at the surface; fix the vessel condition first
npsh.warnFlashing: NPSHa ≤ 0 — the liquid flashes before reaching the impeller; a pump cannot operate here
npsh.footnote: NPSHa = (P_surface − P_v)/(ρ·g) + z − h_f with g = 9.80665 m/s² exactly — a first-principles head balance at the impeller centerline, not a standard's method. z is the liquid level above the centerline (negative for a suction lift); h_f is the suction-line friction head (the ΔP card's frictional term is a good source). The water helper uses IAPWS-IF97: Pv = p_sat(T) (Region 4) and ρ = ρ_f(T), the saturated-liquid density (Region 1 on the saturation line), valid 0–350 °C. This card deliberately renders NO verdict: the required margin over NPSHr belongs to the pump vendor's curve and the Hydraulic Institute / API 610 margin guidance, which are licensed documents this application does not reproduce.

cmp.title: Compressor — Head & Power
cmp.zNote: Z₁ / Z₂ / Z_avg — Z₂ at the one-pass T₂ estimate
cmp.pathNote: pressure ratio · polytropic exponent n · implied isentropic efficiency
cmp.warnNoCompression: P₂ must exceed P₁ — this card screens compression only.
cmp.warnPapaySuction: Suction state outside Papay validity (Pr = {pr}, Tr = {trv}; valid 0 < Pr ≤ 15, 1.05 ≤ Tr ≤ 3.0) — Z₁ is an extrapolation.
cmp.warnPapayDischarge: Discharge state outside Papay validity (Pr = {pr}, Tr = {trv}) — Z₂ is an extrapolation.
cmp.footnote: First-principles screening: H_poly = Z_avg·(R/M)·T₁·(r^m − 1)/m with m = (k−1)/(k·η_p), and H_is with m_s = (k−1)/k — the textbook isentropic and perfect-gas polytropic relations, not a performance-test procedure (ASME PTC 10 is a licensed test code and is not used here). Real-gas correction enters through Z_avg = (Z₁ + Z₂)/2 from the same Papay correlation as the Z-Factor card; Z₂ is evaluated once at the perfect-gas discharge estimate T₂ = T₁·r^m, a deterministic single pass. T₂ is the perfect-gas polytropic path temperature — real-gas and cooling effects will shift the actual value. Gas power = ṁ·H_poly/η_p, the enthalpy rise rate only: add mechanical losses (bearings, seals, gearbox) per the vendor. Unit factors are exact by definition: 1 ft·lbf/lbm = 9.80665 × 0.3048 = 2.98906692 J/kg; 1 hp = 550 ft·lbf/s = 745.69987 W. Typical polytropic efficiencies run ≈ 70–85 % for centrifugal machines — use the vendor's number when you have it.

deltaP.title: Pipe Delta Pressure Calculator
deltaP.cfactorTooltip: API RP 14E erosional-velocity constant C. Use 100 for continuous service, 125 for intermittent, higher for solids-free corrosion-resistant lines.
deltaP.erosionalVeTooltip: API RP 14E erosional velocity limit Ve = C/√ρ
deltaP.enterFlowRate: Enter at least one flow rate
deltaP.regimeNoteWithResult: Two-phase flow regime: {regime} (θ = {theta}°). Re-run Visualize Flow Regime below if inputs changed.
deltaP.regimeNoteNoResult: Two-phase mixture — use the Flow Regime card below to classify the flow pattern.
deltaP.regimeNoteFromViz: Two-phase flow regime: {regime} (θ = {theta}°, v_mix = {vmix} m/s).
deltaP.fittingsNote: Crane TP-410 resistance coefficients, K = n·f_T, where f_T is the fully-turbulent friction factor for the nearest nominal size. Entrance and exit are direct K values with no n. Leave all counts at 0 to exclude fittings entirely.
deltaP.lineSizingTooltip: NORSOK P-001 sizing criteria — screening only
deltaP.lineSizingFootnote: Line-sizing limits are NORSOK P-001 §6.3.2/§6.4 and Tables 3–4, applied to the frictional ΔP only (static head is excluded — it is not a sizing criterion). Gas: v_max = min(175·ρ^−0.43, 60) m/s. Two-phase: v_max = min(183·ρ_mix^−0.5, 25) m/s non-corrosive, 10 m/s corrosive. Liquid velocity bands are material-dependent; Cu-Ni is the lowest at 3 m/s because of seawater erosion. Pump-circuit limits are ΔP-based. Screening guidance for line sizing — not a substitute for a full hydraulic study, and independent of the API RP 14E erosional check above.

psv.title: PRV Sizing Calculator
psv.gasInfoBox: P1 = Set Pressure × (1 + OP%) + P_atm. Critical vs. Subcritical auto-detected: Pcf = P1 × (2/(k+1))^(k/(k−1)).
psv.steamInfoBox: KN (Napier correction) is computed automatically. KSH = 1.0 for saturated steam; use Table 9 in API 520 for superheated values.
psv.twophaseInfoBox: v9 = specific volume from isenthalpic (adiabatic) flash to 0.9×Po — obtain from process simulator. SI: vo/v9 in m³/kg; Po/Pa in kPa abs.
psv.disclaimer: ⚠ Preliminary sizing only per API 520 §5.6–§5.10. Final PRV selection requires independent engineering review, manufacturer-certified Kd, and compliance with applicable codes (ASME, local regulations).
psv.detailsPlaceholder: Run calculation to see intermediate values (C, Pcf, KN, ω, η_c, G, Kv, Re…)
psv.advisorySuperheated: Entered T is {dt} {u} above saturation — superheated steam: take KSH from API 520 Table 9.
psv.advisorySaturated: Entered T is at/below saturation — saturated steam: KSH = 1.0.
